summary: Rye sprouts are appearing unevenly. Keep unsprouted areas moist and assess coverage before adding seed.

cards.name: New rye lawn
cards.action: Keep the seedbed moist with gentle watering while unsprouted areas continue germinating. Skip runs where soil is already wet. Do not reduce watering across the entire lawn just because a few areas sprouted; keep the old two-hour program off.
cards.amount: Enough to moisten the seedbed without puddles or runoff; sprinkler output has not been measured.
cards.frequency: Check around 7 AM, 11 AM, 2 PM and 5 PM; water only as needed to prevent the seedbed drying, without runoff.
cards.nextCheck: Recheck coverage around November 8. Share a photo of thin and bare areas before deciding on spot seeding.
cards.why: First sprouts are confirmed in some areas. Uneven emergence does not yet establish which areas failed after the flooding.

cards.name: Green hopseed
cards.action: Check moisture inside the original root ball daily. Hand-water slowly when it begins drying, keeping it moist rather than soggy.
cards.amount: Wet the root ball and nearby soil; an exact volume needs a moisture and delivery check.
cards.frequency: Daily moisture checks this first week; watering is conditional, not automatically daily.
cards.nextCheck: Review a twice-weekly drip starting plan around November 11.
cards.why: New shrub roots need reliable moisture. Nursery container size is not a watering dose.

cards.name: Barrel & totem cactus
cards.action: Do not repeat routine watering yet. Keep emitters closed if the shared zone would water them too often.
cards.frequency: Check soil dryness before the next watering; do not put them on automatic twice-weekly watering.
cards.nextCheck: November 11 is a soil check, not an automatic watering date.
cards.why: They were watered at planting; damaged roots need time to heal and wet soil can promote rot.

cards.name: Moroccan mound
cards.action: Keep it on a separate low-water approach from the hopseed. Let soil dry between waterings.
cards.amount: Avoid saturating the root area repeatedly; exact delivery is not yet calibrated.
cards.frequency: Check soil first; no automatic extra hand-watering while wet.
cards.nextCheck: Review soil moisture before connecting it to a frequent shared drip schedule.
cards.why: This is a succulent, not a shrub that should stay steadily moist.

cards.name: Hybrid fan & Mediterranean fan palms
cards.action: Check root-zone moisture before a drip run. Do not increase watering simply because new plants were added.
cards.amount: Recorded baseline: about 24 gallons per palm per run; this has not been validated against root-zone wetting.
cards.frequency: Recorded baseline: about every four days. Skip or adjust when soil is already wet.
cards.nextCheck: Check the root area before the next scheduled run.
cards.why: Emitter flow controls volume, but every plant on a valve shares its watering days.

tasks.title: First rye fertilizer
tasks.instruction: Planned first rye feeding: 1.54 lb total of plain Scotts Starter 24-25-4, with Scotts drop setting 6 subject to the actual bag/model. Apply only once, provided seedlings are established and conditions are suitable. If starter was already applied at seeding, skip this additional feeding.

tasks.title: Lawn recovery check
tasks.instruction: Compare sprouted and bare areas after a few more days. Check for seed piles and washed-out streaks; share a photo before adding seed. Do not rake through the new sprouts.

tasks.title: New plant drip review
tasks.instruction: Review hopseed establishment and each plant’s moisture before changing the shared zone. Cacti may remain on manual watering.
